html:
Hendrik Witbooi was a leader of the Nama in southern Namibia, who fought German rule and died in battle in 1905.

A Christian and a gifted letter writer, he fought for years to unite the Nama and against the Herero. He refused to accept German protection, arguing in his letters that he was an independent ruler. After Germans attacked his base at Hornkranz in 1893, he fought them until 1894, then signed a treaty and served them as an ally.

In October 1904, after the Herero rising, he turned against the Germans again, at about 74. He was killed in October 1905, and the Nama were sent to camps in the genocide. His portrait is on the banknotes of Namibia, and his letters are a rare African record of German conquest.
